facts.text: Tudor City is named for its Tudor Revival architecture and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The site of Tudor City was once part of the Turtle Bay Farm, originally called Prospect Hill because it overlooked the East River.
Tudor City's private parks originally followed the precedent of Gramercy Park, where only residents could receive keys for entry.
The overpass carrying Tudor City Place above 42nd Street is a popular spot for photos of the Manhattanhenge solar alignment.
Actor Charlton Heston once lived in one of the penthouses at Tudor City.
The Sharansky Steps in Tudor City honor Soviet dissident Natan Sharansky and lead down to Ralph Bunche Park.
